firewallPage.appliedCounts: Applied. {{added}} rule(s) put on the router, {{removed}} taken off, {{unchanged}} already there.
firewallPage.appliedNoChange: The router already had exactly these rules. Nothing needed to change.
firewallPage.applyEffect: It takes effect straight away: traffic that matches a Block rule stops, including for guests already connected. Nothing else on the router is changed.
firewallPage.applyNone: No rule is switched on, so the router will be left with none of your rules.
firewallPage.applyOff: {{off}} switched-off rule(s), and any rule you deleted, will be taken off the router.
firewallPage.applyOn: The router will get the {{on}} switched-on rule(s) listed here, checked in the order shown ({{blocks}} of them Block).
firewallPage.applyUnpushable: {{count}} switched-on rule(s) protect the router itself and can't be applied from here, so the router will refuse this change until they are switched off.
firewallPage.bandMissing: This router hasn't been prepared for firewall rules yet. Our team needs to set it up once — contact support.
firewallPage.bandReady: This router is ready for firewall rules.
firewallPage.bypassBody: Without this, a guest who changes their phone's DNS (like 8.8.8.8 or Private DNS) can still open blocked websites.
firewallPage.bypassFailed: The last change to this didn't work.
firewallPage.bypassOnToast: Guests can no longer get around the blocks.
firewallPage.bypassTitle: Stop guests getting around these blocks
firewallPage.deleteActive: This rule is on the router now. Deleting it here removes it from this list; it comes off the router the next time you apply.
firewallPage.deletePending: This rule is not on the router, so deleting it changes nothing there.
firewallPage.demoBody: Firewall rules are written to a real router, and the demo account has none.
firewallPage.demoTitle: Not part of the demo account
firewallPage.formHint: Save keeps the rule here without changing the router. Save and apply puts your rules on the router straight away, including for guests already connected.
firewallPage.intro: Block a website by typing its name, or decide which devices on your network may reach which addresses. Address rules are checked top first, and nothing changes on your router until you apply them.
firewallPage.namePlaceholder: e.g. Keep guests off the office printer
firewallPage.noRouterBody: This venue has no router yet.
firewallPage.noRouterTitle: No router here can take firewall rules
firewallPage.noRules: No rules yet. Without any, the router lets your network's traffic through as it does today.
firewallPage.notAppliedHint: {{count}} rule(s) are saved but not on the router. They take effect when you apply them.
firewallPage.placeAllow: Allow rules go to the top of the list, so they win over your Block rules.
firewallPage.placeBlock: New Block rules go to the bottom of the list.
firewallPage.privateBody: Guests can use the internet but can't reach your office computers, billing machine, cameras or your internet box's settings page.
firewallPage.privateFailed: Couldn't change this. Nothing was applied to the router.
firewallPage.privateTitle: Keep guests off your private networks
firewallPage.savedToast: Saved. Apply to router when you're ready.
firewallPage.siteCategoriesPrefix: Want to block whole kinds of sites (adult, gambling, …)? Use
firewallPage.siteHint: Type the name — no address needed. It's blocked by name on the router (DNS), including every page and subdomain of it.
firewallPage.siteInvalid: Type a website name like youtube.com. To block an address, add a rule below.
firewallPage.siteSavedNotPushed: {{site}} was saved but didn't reach the router, so it isn't blocked yet. Press retry on it.
firewallPage.siteUnblockFailed: Couldn't reach the router, so {{site}} is still blocked. Try again.
firewallPage.whoSpecific: A specific device or group of devices
firewallPage.floodBody: Stops one guest device from opening hundreds of connections at once, which is how flood attacks and password-guessing tools work. Strict limits can break busy apps such as cloud backup, video calls and big downloads.
firewallPage.floodCustom: This router has a custom limit of {{n}} connections per device. Pick a level to replace it.
firewallPage.floodPartial: Part of this limit is missing on the router. Choose a level again to repair it.
firewallPage.floodNeedsBand: This can be turned on once the router has been prepared for firewall rules.
firewallPage.floodOnToast: Connection-flood limit applied to the router.
firewallPage.floodOffToast: Connection-flood limit removed from the router.
firewallPage.siteHttpsHint: It's also blocked by name on secure (https) connections, which catches most phones that skip the router's DNS. Nothing is decrypted. A browser that hides the site's name, or a newer kind of connection (QUIC), can still get through.
firewallPage.devicesLoading: Loading the devices on your network…
firewallPage.devicesFailed: Couldn't load the devices on your network. Use “A specific address or range” instead, or try again in a minute.
firewallPage.devicesNone: We haven't seen any devices on this router yet. Devices appear here a few minutes after they connect.
firewallPage.devicesSearch: Search by name, address or MAC
firewallPage.keepStopsMatching: If this device's address changes, this rule will stop matching it.
firewallPage.guestWhoNote: This is a guest's device. Guests' addresses change and are handed to the next guest, so this rule may soon match someone else. To keep one guest device off your WiFi, use
firewallPage.guestWhoTail: — it blocks the device itself, not its address.
firewallPage.keepChecking: Checking whether this device keeps its address…
firewallPage.keepAddress: Keep this device on the same address
firewallPage.keepAddressHint: Recommended. The router will always give {{name}} {{ip}}, so this rule keeps matching it.
firewallPage.keepAlready: The router always gives this device {{ip}}.
firewallPage.keepCannot: This device didn't get its address from the router, so we can't keep it fixed from here.
firewallPage.keepUnknown: We couldn't check whether this device keeps its address.
firewallPage.keepFailed: Couldn't keep this device on its address.
firewallPage.pickDevice: Pick a device from the list.
firewallPage.deviceMoved: {{name}} is now at {{ip}}. Saving moves this rule to its new address.
firewallPage.deviceNotSeen: We can't see this device on the router right now, so the rule keeps using {{ip}}.
firewallPage.whereNoGuests: Guests' devices aren't listed here: their addresses change and are handed to the next guest.
firewallPage.devicesTruncated: Showing the first 500 devices. Search narrows these; for anything else, use “A specific address or range”.

webFilteringPage.bypassTitle: Stop guests getting around the filter
webFilteringPage.bypassBody: Stops signed-in guests' devices using their own private lookup service instead of the filter. It can't catch every workaround, and a few apps that insist on their own may not load.
webFilteringPage.bypassNeedsOn: Available once web filtering is on.
webFilteringPage.bypassFailed: The last change to this didn't work.
webFilteringPage.enableWhat: This changes how {{router}} looks up every website, for everyone on its network — guests and your own devices.
webFilteringPage.enableSafety: Straight after the change we check that websites still open. If that check fails, the router switches back to its own settings automatically.
webFilteringPage.disableWhat: The router goes back to the website lookup settings it had before, and the categories on your list stop being blocked.

blockWebsites.advancedHint: For blocking a number like 203.0.113.7 instead of a name, and for seeing every block on each router with its status.
blockWebsites.demoTitle: Not part of the demo account
blockWebsites.demoBody: Blocking a website changes a real router, and the demo account has none.
blockWebsites.noRouterTitle: No router here can block websites
blockWebsites.noRouterBody: This venue has no router yet.
blockWebsites.siteInvalid: Type a website name like youtube.com. To block an internet address, open Advanced at the bottom of this page.
blockWebsites.firewallIntro: Decide which devices on your network may reach which internet addresses. Rules are checked top first, and nothing changes on your router until you apply them.
blockWebsites.firewallWebsitesPrefix: To block a website by its name, use

blockWebsites.dialogBody: Block a website (and every page under it) or an internet address on this router's guest WiFi.

harmfulSites.title: Block known harmful websites (recommended)
harmfulSites.body: Stops guests opening websites Cloudflare knows spread viruses or steal passwords (malware and phishing). Cloudflare keeps the list up to date.
harmfulSites.ownList: This venue uses your account's list. Changing this gives the venue its own list.
harmfulSites.onToast: Known harmful websites are on this venue's list.
harmfulSites.offToast: Known harmful websites are no longer on the list.

harmfulSites.stepNeeded: One step left at {{router}}: turn on web filtering there, or nothing on this list is blocked.

link.categories: Choose kinds of website to block

label.domain_blocking_sni: Block a website on secure (HTTPS) connections
label.rogue_dhcp_detection: Warn me about an unknown router on my network
label.connection_flood_protection: Limit connection floods and password guessing
label.dns_bypass_protection: Stop guests getting round website blocks

copy.domain_blocking_sni: Block a website by name on secure (https) connections too, without opening or reading anyone's traffic. It is switched on with every website you block, but we have not yet proven it on a real router, so it is listed here until we have. It cannot see a site whose browser hides the name, or newer kinds of connection (QUIC), or a VPN.
copy.application_control: Switch off apps such as YouTube, Instagram or BGMI on your guest WiFi. It blocks the website names each app uses, not the app itself, so some apps may still get through -- one that is already open, one with a built-in address, or a phone with its own DNS or a VPN.
copy.threat_intelligence: Stop guests opening websites known to spread viruses or steal passwords. Cloudflare keeps the list up to date. It works on routers where web filtering is on, and a phone with its own DNS or a VPN is not covered.

blockGuests.deviceHint: Paste one or more device (Wi-Fi/MAC) addresses separated by commas. Your router cuts the device off now and every time it reconnects.
blockGuests.deviceMacNote: Anonymous guests can switch on a private Wi-Fi address on their phone and come back as a new device, so use this for devices you know.
blockGuests.deviceConfirmBody: Your router will drop these devices now and every time they reconnect, until you unblock them.
